spatial_claims.claim: O is the center of the circle; A is on the circumference; OA is a radius
Equilateral triangles OAB and OAF constructed on opposite sides of line OA
B lies on the circle since OB = OA = radius; F lies on the circle since OF = OA = radius
angle AOB = angle AOF = alpha, with 3*alpha = two right angles (so alpha = 60 degrees)
AO produced through O meets circle at D (AD is a diameter); BO produced through O meets circle at E (BE is a diameter); FO produced through O meets circle at C (FC is a diameter)
OC and OF are opposite rays since F-O-C are collinear (FC is a diameter)
angle AOC + angle AOF = two right angles (supplementary angles on straight line FC)
angle AOC = 2*alpha (subtracting angle AOF = alpha from two right angles = 3*alpha)
B and C are both on the side of diameter AD opposite to F
Ray OB lies inside angle AOC (since alpha < 2*alpha and B, C on same side of AD)
angle AOC = angle AOB + angle BOC, so angle BOC = alpha
Vertical angles: angle COD = angle FOA, angle DOE = angle AOB, angle EOF = angle BOC (all equal alpha)
Vertices occur in cyclic order A, B, C, D, E, F around the circle; all six central angles equal alpha
All six radial triangles (OAB, OBC, OCD, ODE, OEF, OFA) have two sides equal to the radius and included angle alpha; by SAS they are congruent
At each vertex, the interior angle of the hexagon equals the sum of the base angles of two adjacent radial triangles: alpha + alpha = 2*alpha

configuration_map: Six points A, B, C, D, E, F equally spaced on a circle with center O, each separated by central angle alpha = 60 degrees. Three diameters AD, BE, FC all pass through O. Going around the circle from A: B is at 60 degrees, C at 120 degrees, D at 180 degrees (diametrically opposite A), E at 240 degrees, F at 300 degrees. B and F are on opposite sides of diameter AD (constructed as equilateral triangles on opposite sides of radius OA). C is diametrically opposite F, so C is on the same side of AD as B. E is diametrically opposite B. The center O is inside the hexagon, and from any vertex the ray to O falls between the two sides of the hexagon, validating the interior angle decomposition.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The equilateral triangle construction on the radius correctly places B and F on the circle on opposite sides of OA. The diameter extensions correctly place C opposite F and E opposite B. The angle arithmetic (supplementary angles, vertical angles, additive decomposition with OB between OA and OC) is valid throughout. The interior angle decomposition at each vertex is valid because O lies inside the regular hexagon. No configuration contradictions found.
